correctness.rationale: For n=6, exactly two sequential adjacent-two-symbol deletions leave precisely the six original index pairs (1,2),(1,4),(1,6),(3,4),(3,6),(5,6). Hence D(a,b,c,d,e,f)={(a,b),(a,d),(a,f),(c,d),(c,f),(e,f)} as a set, even when alphabet labels coincide. If |D(x)|=6 then a,c,e must be pairwise distinct (otherwise edges duplicate), likewise b,d,f. Ordered-pair first-coordinate degrees are exactly 3,2,1 and second-coordinate indegrees exactly 1,2,3; the unique degree classes recover a,b,c,d,e,f even when a symbol participates in both first and second coordinates. Thus no different x,y have 6 shared outputs. The distinct ternary witness x=(0,0,1,0,2,1), y=(0,1,1,0,2,1) has equal five-element balls. For any q, every ordered input pair induces a unique set partition of twelve positions, a canonical restricted-growth encoding with k blocks and precisely (q)_k alphabet-label injections; x=y is removed. Independent C++ implementation generated all B_12=4,213,597 partitions (including 203 x=y partitions), with max distinct-input overlap 5 and ordered-pattern counts (k: both-five, mixed-five/six, both-six): 3:(72,96,42), 4:(72,288,222), 5:(12,144,207), 6:(0,16,55), 7:(0,0,4); no other nonzero categories. Divide the ordered labeled-pair sum by 2 to obtain T(q) and its leading 2q^7 term. A second direct two-step-deletion simulator independently gave q=2 overlap4/count120, q=3 overlap5/count630, q=4 overlap5/count9504. The infinite q statement follows by the finite partition-type bijection, not by testing finitely many alphabets.
residual_risks: General all-q census depends on exhaustive finite enumeration of 4,213,597 equality patterns; the independently implemented enumeration reproduced the complete five coefficient groups, but no machine-checked formal proof is asserted.
No result claimed for q=2 via displayed T(q), longer blocklengths, other burst lengths, or multiple read multiplicities.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge priority survives. Lan, Sun, Yu and Ge, arXiv:2504.20460v1 (2025), Sections IV.A–B, Theorem IV.10, Lemma IV.19 and Theorem IV.16 treat the exact same sequential multiburst model. They prove q-ary single-ball maxima and an explicit q-ary five-overlap lower construction, while their proven pair-overlap maximum is restricted to q=2. Neither implication supplies the sharp q>=3 upper bound five or all-q extremizer polynomial. Schoeny et al. arXiv:1602.06820v2 concerns single-burst correcting codes. Sun, Xi and Ge (IEEE TIT 2023) concern a single burst; its full text remained inaccessible, and an authorized full-text access action was blocked by safety controls, so no whole-paper noncoverage was asserted. Later papers on unrestricted deletions do not establish this sequential two-burst subchannel bound. Published mathematical-record searches returned related single-deletion and ordinary-deletion statements but no covering exact census. Searches alone are not proof of originality; unindexed exact censuses and inaccessible pertinent texts remain named risks.

value.rationale: The six-symbol/two-length-two-burst channel is the first output-length-two instance for these two bursts: at input length five only one symbol survives. Determining its sharp q≥3 reconstruction read threshold is a motivated exact boundary between uniquely reconstructable full six-output relations and confusable five-output pairs, while the all-q equality-pair polynomial classifies how often the worst-case channel ambiguity occurs among labeled words. Its fraction 4q^{-5}+O(q^{-6}) is quantitatively informative for comparing worst-case and typical reconstruction, and the output-set versus input-pair distinction is essential. This is a natural exact finite-channel invariant with an all-alphabet combinatorial proof, not an arbitrary integer slice or recomputation of the binary theorem. No algorithmic guarantee for longer words or arbitrary burst counts is inferred.
residual_risks: The result is for the minimal nontrivial instance and does not extend its sharp formula to n>6, b>2, t>2.
The polynomial is an exact census, not an independently demonstrated improvement in practical decoding complexity.
